transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

This symptom usually indicates a blocked vent or lint filter causing overheating, which triggers the safety thermostat to cut power until it cools down. You should clean the lint filter and check that the external window vent is not obstructed by debris or bird nests. From what you have described, the most likely cause is clean the lint/fluff filter and clear the fluff build-up. Can you tell me whether filter full of fluff?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
i clean the filter regularly so its not that. the cabinet gets really hot before it stops tho

From what you have described, the most likely cause is thermal cut-out (TOC). Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
its a vented one, no condenser i think. the hose behind is crushed tho, i pushed it back further recently. has fluff in the folds

From what you have described, the most likely cause is check the blower fan turns and is clear. Can you tell me whether fan not turning?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
not sure how to check the fan tbh, dont really want to take it apart its my landlords. is there an easier way to check?

Yes, you can simply inspect the vent hose from outside while the dryer runs to see if air is actually exiting. If no air comes out or the airflow is very weak, the blockage is confirmed without needing to open the machine. A very small load (or one item) can make a sensor dryer finish early, and an overloaded drum can make it overheat. Was the load very small or overloaded (and have you changed it), or was it a normal load?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
its usually big loads, esp full ones, its worse then. ive not checked the air coming out the window tho. when i unhooked the hose into the room it ran the full 40 mins fine

Sensor dryers stop when two metal strips inside the drum (near the filter) feel the laundry is dry. Fabric conditioner can coat them — wipe them with a damp cloth and a little vinegar. Were they coated or dirty (and are they clean now), or were they already clean?
havent checked those strips, not sure where they are tbh. the hose being crushed behind it is the thing i noticed tho. what should i do?

You need to straighten the crushed vent hose and ensure there is a clear path for hot air to escape. Since you are reluctant to open the appliance, fixing the external airflow restriction is the only safe step you can take yourself. Run a normal drying programme and stay nearby. Does it run right through now, or still stop part way?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok will straighten it out n try a normal load. do u want me to tell u if it runs thru?
